currentContext.business: SMIORE mines and sells manganese ore and iron ore from leases in Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karnataka, and upgrades part of that ore into ferroalloys (silicomanganese/ferromanganese) at its Vyasanakere plant, alongside a coke & energy business now run largely under contract manufacturing arrangements. Following the acquisition of material subsidiary Arjas Steel Private Limited and step-down subsidiary Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited, the group also manufactures special bar quality (SBQ)/alloy steel. It operates on a Business-to-Business basis, serving industrial customers — principally steel manufacturers and ferroalloy producers — with captive solar/wind and waste-heat power assets held through separate SPVs supporting the ferroalloys and steel segments.

currentContext.expansion: SMIORE completed all its interim mining expansions in the previous year and FY26 was the first full year of operating at the enhanced Maximum Permissible Annual Production (MPAP) limits of 0.599 MTPA for manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA for iron ore, which delivered highest-ever production and sales in both ores. On a consolidated basis the group now runs four segments with installed capacity of 0.599 MTPA manganese ore and 4.45 MTPA iron ore in Mining, 95,000/1,25,000 TPA of ferroalloys (SiMn/FeMn), 0.50 MTPA of coke with 32 MW of Waste-Heat Recovery Boiler based power, and 0.585 MTPA of steel manufacturing with 21 MW of waste-heat based captive power added through the acquisition of material subsidiary Arjas Steel Private Limited and step-down subsidiary Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited. Two named projects are in flight. First, a 300 tonne-per-hour, 1.2 km Downhill Conveyor Pipe System (DCS) from the Kammathuru iron ore mine to the PMBR railway siding: the proposal is completed, necessary approvals including Consent for Operation - Expansion were obtained during the year, a Forest Lease Agreement was executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Government of Karnataka, Ballari Division, and the system is expected to be operational within H1FY27; it passes through 2.4314 hectares of forest land in the Deogiri Swamimalai Forest Block and is intended to enable environment-friendly ore transportation and fetch better realisations by delivering ore directly to the railway siding, with SMIORE the first private mine in Ballari and Vijayanagara districts to comply with a DCS for ore evacuation in line with Supreme Court directions. Second, a 2.0 MTPA Beneficiation Plant at Deogiri is in the process of being set up to upgrade iron ore grade concentrate suitable for pellet manufacturing, designed to deliver 1.0 to 1.2 MTPA of output using crushing, screening, grinding, magnetic separation and filtration, with the aim of improved realisation through pellet feed quality and reduced waste. Beyond capacity, the Company received Consent for Operation approval on one mining lease to handle incidental iron ore of 0.327 MT by 30 August 2026, permitting sale of already-excavated ore over and above annual production limits. In coke, roughly 46% of Coke Oven capacity (2 of 4 batteries) is committed under a contract manufacturing agreement continued into FY27, and the Company is actively engaging additional customers to recommence the remaining 2 batteries, which would raise utilisation and waste-heat energy generation and in turn support better ferroalloys capacity utilisation in FY27. Captive power is held through SPVs — ReNew Sandur Green Energy Private Limited with 42.9 MW of solar-wind hybrid capacity for ferroalloys and Amplus Arjas Solar Private Limited with 20.4 MW of solar capacity for steel — and the Company had entered into a Share Subscription and Shareholders' Agreement with ReNew Green Energy Solutions (the description of which is truncated in the source text).

risks.risk: Occupational health & safety in a high-risk mining and smelting operation
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: given the high-risk nature of operations, failure to manage safety may result in workplace injuries, regulatory non-compliance, legal penalties and operational disruptions, while exposure to dust, heat and noise creates occupational health risks; incidents also affect workforce morale and reputation. Mitigated through Standard Operating Procedures conforming to ISO 45001:2018, regular training and mock drills, and regular safety audits and inspections.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: non-adherence to governance practices, non-compliance with applicable regulations or unethical business conduct may result in reputational damage, penalties and loss of stakeholder trust, affecting long-term performance. Mitigated via the Employees' Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, training and awareness sessions, a compliance monitoring system and periodic internal and external audits.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: operations involve extensive engagement with employees, contract workers, local communities and other stakeholders, and failure to respect and uphold human rights may lead to regulatory actions, legal disputes, social unrest, operational delays and reputational damage. Mitigated through the POSH policy, a mechanism for raising concerns and resolving disputes, just and favourable working conditions and advocacy of gender equality.

FY26 was a muted year from a realisations standpoint, with prices across both manganese ore and iron ore bottoming out in Q2FY26 and Q3FY26; the year-to-date average spot price for 44% grade manganese ore from China was down 22% in October 2025 against the 2024 annual average, and the USGS-reported 62% Fe fines price averaged below the prior-year level. Realisations, not volumes, drove the softness in FY26 and remain outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Dependence on the global and domestic steel cycle
risks.note: Roughly 96% of manganese ore consumption is directed into steelmaking, so demand closely follows steel output. Global crude steel output declined for a second consecutive year in 2025 (down 1.1% to 1.93 billion tonnes) on persistent Chinese property-sector weakness, and global finished steel consumption was unchanged, weighing directly on manganese and iron ore prices. A prolonged steel downcycle transmits straight into the Company's mining and ferroalloys segments.

risks.risk: Geographic, asset and product concentration with no export offset
risks.note: All mines are located at Deogiri, Subbarayanahalli, Kammathuru and Ramghad in Sandur Taluk, Ballari District, Karnataka, with a single plant at Vyasanakere, Mariyammanahalli, Hosapete, Vijayanagara District. The BRSR records no international plants, offices or markets and exports as Nil percent of total turnover, so the business is fully exposed to a single mining district and to domestic demand. Product mix is also concentrated: mining accounts for 76.22% of standalone turnover, with iron ore alone at 65.12%.

risks.risk: Regulatory and approval dependence on mining limits, environmental consents and forest land
risks.note: Output is capped by Maximum Permissible Annual Production limits, and expansion and evacuation infrastructure depend on approvals such as Consent for Operation and Consent for Operation - Expansion plus a Forest Lease Agreement executed with the Deputy Conservator of Forests for the DCS crossing 2.4314 hectares of forest land; the DCS itself is being set up in line with directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Any delay or adverse change in these approvals directly constrains volumes and project timelines. Regulatory change also hits costs — new Labour Codes notified by the Government of India gave rise to an exceptional item in FY26.

risks.risk: Macro and geopolitical supply shock raising energy and input costs
risks.note: The MD&A flags that downside risks dominate the outlook: the West Asia conflict is a negative supply shock, with the assumed oil price rising to about $82 per barrel in 2026, elevated energy, fertiliser and industrial input prices, a wholesale price index that rose from 2.1% in February to 3.9% in March 2026 signalling cost-push pressures, and adverse/severe scenarios in which global growth falls to 2.5% or 1.8% in 2026. A longer or broader conflict, deeper geopolitical fragmentation or renewed trade tensions could weaken growth and destabilise financial markets.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
